title: introduce-econ-ci-guardian-simulated-workload-check-and-gate
author: Maya Singh
description:
Motivation: accidental PRs can introduce cost regressions (larger batch shapes, disabled caching, or quantization toggles) that are invisible to unit tests but show up in production spend. This PR adds an automated CI guard that runs a small simulated workload on new PRs and computes per-tenant unit-econ deltas against a baseline. If the cost delta crosses configured soft/hard thresholds the PR is annotated and can be blocked.

What this change does: adds a lightweight simulator (pkg/econ/sim) and a new CLI (cmd/econ-checker) used by a GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/econ-check.yml). The workflow runs on PRs, performs three short synthetic traces (latency/seq-dist/rd), captures token counts and approximate GPU-seconds, and computes an expected per-1M-token cost delta with the existing baseline for the model+config. The tool posts an automated review comment with a concise cost-impact summary and creates a check run that can be configured as required for release branches.

Key behaviors: the check is designed to be conservative and fast (wall time ~90s on a small runner); it uses cached reference traces stored in tools/econ-samples and supports tenant-scoped baselines so teams with dedicated capacity can opt in. The gate has two thresholds: a soft warning (default +8% cost) and a hard failure (default +20%). Thresholds are tenant-configurable via .github/econ-config.yml or repo-level defaults. The PR also adds a dry-run mode used by local devs and CI matrix runs.

Files included: .github/workflows/econ-check.yml, cmd/econ-checker/main.go, pkg/econ/sim/simulator.go, pkg/econ/checker.go, tools/econ-samples/README.md, tools/econ-samples/reference-traces.json (small synthetic traces), docs/dev/PR-cost-guidelines.md, integrations/econ/check_integration_test.go

Checklist: 
- [x] Simulator and cost-diff algorithm implemented
- [x] GitHub Actions workflow that posts check runs and comments
- [x] Integrations tests exercising a failure and a pass path
- [x] Documentation and opt-out knobs for tenant owners
- [x] Added Linear tickets and rollout notes (ENG-3245, ENG-4190)

Rollout plan: Merge to main as an opt-in check. Over the next two weeks we'll enable as required on the release/* branches and then gate on main for selected repos. Ops will watch the first 24h of gate failures and create exceptions or tune thresholds per-tenant.

Backward compatibility: The runtime surface of the serving layer is unchanged. The CI check is non-invasive; teams can opt out by adding repo-level config.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the cost model in pkg/econ/checker.go (simple linear cost per-token + small fixed overhead). This intentionally favors interpretability; a follow-up will integrate the internal price oracle. The integration test includes a synthetic regression to validate blocking behavior.

release_notes:
- Add econ CI guardian that simulates short workloads and flags cost regressions
- New CLI `econ-checker` and GitHub Actions workflow to gate PRs for cost impact
- Tenant-configurable thresholds and opt-out
- Integration tests and developer docs for local dry-run
